data.name: Alric
data.gender_notes: Alric is used as a male name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: From the Old High German words ‘al’ meaning ‘all’ and ‘ric’ meaning ‘ruler’ or ‘rich’. This name was borne by several early Christian saints and has a regal and noble feel. The name Alric carries the meaning “Ruler, Rich” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Alric usually hope their child will grow to embody ruler, rich and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Emblematic of divine leadership and guidance.
data.etymology: Alric belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Ruler, Rich.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Alric total 7, giving a life-path number of 7. Number 7 is linked with Ketu and with the qualities of reflection, wisdom and inner depth.
data.cultural_impact: Alaric I, a famous king of the Visigoths in the late 5th century CE, is well known for sacking Rome in 410 CE. Likely due to the powerful name and associations with ruling and prosperity, "Alaric" became popular among Western Europeans in the Middle Ages.
data.spiritual_significance: In the Christian tradition, St. Alaricius, an Anglo-Saxon hermit, is venerated for his piety and commitment to a celibate life. The name can be seen as a reminder of the spiritual richness and rulership that comes from living a God-centered life.
